title: How to protect your car's paint through a Calgary winter
description: What brine, mag chloride, gravel and cold do to car paint in Calgary, and the steps that keep a finish in shape from November to March.
excerpt: Brine and mag chloride attack paint chemically, gravel attacks it physically, and the cold makes washing harder. The steps that get a finish through to spring.

sections.heading: Protect before the first snow
paragraphs: Anything you put on the paint has to be on before the roads turn white. A sealant or ceramic coating gives salt and mag chloride something to sit on besides the clear coat, and makes every winter wash easier.

sections.heading: Wash on the warm days
paragraphs: Mag chloride stays damp and keeps working well below freezing. Rinse the vehicle, including the wheel wells and lower panels, whenever there's a stretch above zero. A touchless rinse is better than letting it sit.

sections.heading: Watch the front end
paragraphs: Traction gravel at highway speed chips bumpers, hood edges and mirrors. Coatings don't stop impacts. If the vehicle is new or you're keeping it long-term, film on the high-impact areas is the only real defence.

sections.heading: Don't forget the inside
paragraphs: Salt walks in on boots and dries into white rings on the carpet. Rubber floor liners catch most of it, and a deep interior clean in spring removes what got through before it stiffens and stains the fibres.
